scope: Bounded audit of §12.8.3.2 PKCS #1; §12.8.3.3.2 CMS revocation attribute; §12.8.3.4.2 PAdES signature-dictionary constraints; and §§12.8.3.4.6-.8 CRL/OCSP revocation at current and past validation times. Prior §12.8.3.4.5 open-trigger and §12.8.5 DTS/DocMDP carveout reviews are not repeated.

features.title: PKCS #1 signatures
features.source: EC3 primary printed p.578 (physical p.593), adjacent Table 260 and §12.8.3.2 paragraph
effective_rules: PKCS #1 PDF signatures are deprecated in PDF 2.0
The only SubFilter that should be used is adbe.x509.rsa_sha1; signer certificate chain shall be in /Cert
features.implementation: Legacy reader verifies the raw PKCS #1 signature against certificate in /Cert, reports missing or incompatible key; host trust-anchor path is separate from cryptographic verification.
assertions: signature.rs has direct key match, no-certificate, cryptographic positive and wrong-key controls
trust/verdict tests use supplied anchor and preserve identity/trust distinction
features.status_review: Implemented support for this deprecated legacy format is consistent with reader interoperability; producer-facing should/deprecation language is not a reader-side mandate to reject it.
caveats: Do not call the self-contained signer certificate chain trusted without a host-supplied anchor
PKCS #1 format support does not imply DSA/ECDSA support in this subfilter: Table 260 says no

features.title: Revocation of CMS-based signatures
features.source: EC3 primary printed p.580 (physical p.595), ASN.1 grammar and text
effective_rules: Source applies its producer rule to SubFilter other than ETSI.CAdES.detached
RevocationInfoArchival attribute OID is printed
Grammar permits optional explicit CRL and OCSP sequences plus otherRevInfo
otherRevInfo encoding is OCTET STRING and format/type interpretation is left application dependent
features.implementation: revocation::archived reads CRLs/OCSPs from signed attributes; merges with DSS material; skips unsupported otherRevInfo; status checks against issuer/path per RFC 5280/6960 with Unknown as default.
assertions: Revocation module has strong direct CRL/OCSP cryptographic and status vectors with Good/Revoked/Unknown controls
No direct test was found calling archived() or proving a CMS signed attribute routes its CRL/OCSP into status(); ledger cites status tests, not attribute extraction
features.status_review: Code path exists; direct extraction-to-status assertion gap. Parser-level positive/negative draft included, with intentionally limited claim: it tests attribute routing and reuses independently tested CRL verification, not full valid CMS signature binding.
caveats: The source's non-CAdES clause is a producer condition; reader reading an attribute outside that range is not itself a conformance error
Custom otherRevInfo interpretation is not standardized; skipping it is not evidence of parsing an unknown custom format

features.title: PAdES signature dictionary
features.source: EC3 primary printed pp.581-582 (physical pp.596-597), first paragraph
effective_rules: ETSI.CAdES.detached Contents is DER-encoded CMS SignedData
ByteRange covers entire file except Contents and includes signature dictionary
Cert key prohibited
signing time is in /M or signing-time attribute but not both
features.implementation: pades_departures checks DER status, whole-file/Contents exclusion, Cert, dual signing times, and DER is also enforced where it affects digest interpretation.
assertions: signature.rs::a_pades_signature_is_held_to_the_rules_that_need_no_certificate has explicit conforming and departing control
signature.rs::a_pades_signature_is_held_to_every_attribute_rule_that_needs_no_certificate and encoding tests assert individual consequences
features.status_review: No gap found in this clause's dictionary-level assertions. Departure reporting and signature cryptographic validity remain separate.
caveats: BER outside signed/authenticated attribute DER-only area is reportable source departure but remains readable; do not collapse into failed signature math

features.title: PAdES revocation model
effective_rules: Handler shall use CRLs, OCSP, or both, to check every certificate in path
Inputs are identified using validation parameters
Time modes: current UTC or past UTC when qualifying timestamp token is present
After signer certificate expiry is a separate LTV clause
features.implementation: Trust::Search performs revocation checking per certificate along a successfully validated path; uses document material only; CRL and OCSP paths support issuer/responder authorization, freshness and signed assertions.
assertions: revocation/tests.rs asserts CRL and OCSP Good/Revoked, stale/invalid signature/issuer use, not-covered Unknown
trust/tests.rs asserts path revocation composes through path
no network lookup is performed; document-carrying material and host anchors remain separate
features.status_review: The delegated source and assertions support the method set, path coverage and conservative Unknown status. No valid gap found in this row by itself.
caveats: The local input set restricts methods to document-carried CRLs/OCSP and host-supplied validation context; it does not fetch network responders
No trust-store configuration is inferred from a PDF

features.title: Revocation at current UTC time
effective_rules: Current check is before expiry of signer's certificate and checks each cert in signer's path
CRL appropriate only if now lies in thisUpdate-to-nextUpdate interval
OCSP response appropriate only if captured before expiry of signer's certificate
features.implementation: Revocation status functions take caller instant; CRL code does not reject a current instant before thisUpdate. Neither the shared revocation Subject nor from_response receives the signer's notAfter, so the OCSP captured-before-expiry condition is not enforced at this layer. The same generic status check is used whether the instant is host current time or an authenticated past timestamp.
assertions: Fixed-time revocation fixtures assert literal timestamps, current Good/Revoked, stale CRL -> Unknown, untrusted issuer -> Unknown
No assertion found for a current-time CRL whose thisUpdate is after now
No assertion found for OCSP response captured after the signer's notAfter; current leaf-status tests do not establish this PAdES-specific condition
features.status_review: Two source-to-code gaps: .7 requires current UTC within both thisUpdate and nextUpdate, but from_list has no lower-bound check; it also requires OCSP response capture before signer expiry, but the revocation evaluator has no signer expiry input. The existing future-issued CRL test can support historical-time semantics only; it is not a valid current-time oracle. Keep current/past mode and certificate-expiry context distinct.
caveats: OCSP thisUpdate and producedAt are distinct; the source's capture cutoff must not be inferred from thisUpdate. producedAt is the response-generation timestamp available in the parsed response, but capture semantics should be confirmed before a test equates them

The CRL lower-bound condition is explicit in EC3 §12.8.3.4.7 even though the implementation comments cite a one-ended freshness interpretation from ETSI EN 319 102-1; source priority / adopted scope should be resolved explicitly

features.title: Revocation at a past time
effective_rules: A present signature-timestamp token requires signer signature verification at token UTC time and revocation checking of signer path at that time plus timestamp-authority path
For current status of TSA path, keyCompromise/cACompromise/missing revocation reason invalidates use of token time
Other TSA revocation reasons permit token time only if revocation occurred after token UTC time
CRL captured before signer certificate expiry and nextUpdate later than token time; OCSP captured before signer certificate expiry and producedAt later than token time
features.implementation: Timestamp token establishment reports its path revocation status but declares Time::Established whenever a path reaches an anchor, even if Trust::Anchored carries Revocation::Revoked. notes.rs then takes every Established signature/doc timestamp time as BestSignatureTime without consulting Time.revocation. On signer-path revocation lookup, from_list/from_response also do not receive signer notAfter, so .8's material-captured-before-signer-expiry test cannot be enforced there.
assertions: timestamp tests assert token signature, digest binding, authority anchoring and asked-at semantics; revocation tests assert CRL/OCSP answers and reasons
No inspected assertion covers TSA-path current revocation reason determining whether timestamp genTime is admissible as historical signer-validation time
features.status_review: Parent B41 confirms signature-attribute time selector uses genTime despite known TSA keyCompromise. Document timestamp chain and capture-before-expiry concerns are unexecuted residuals, not confirmed failures.
caveats: `Time::Established` may intentionally expose a cryptographically/path anchored instant while carrying `revocation`; the defect is that callers treating the instant as BestSignatureTime do not apply §12.8.3.4.8's reliability condition
Host acceptance of Unknown revocation does not excuse known Revoked TSA authority status
No network retrieval required; fixture must provide valid signed revocation material and trusted anchor

errata: No EC3 errata annotation was found at the six assigned clause locators. Adjacent errata touching other signature subclauses should not be imported into these findings without checking the actual edited passage.
